note.text: A useful club discussion combines an opinion with a reason and an example. Preferences do not establish universal facts. Ask a precise question when an activity is unclear, and acknowledge another view before responding. A proposal suggests what could happen; it does not report an event already completed. This is written preparation for speaking. A partner or teacher can later assess actual turn-taking, voice and listening, which the screen does not hear.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to express a club preference with reasons, ask for clarification and propose a shared activity. Builds on: family-life discussion, adverbs and letter purpose. Leads to: future plans and argumentative writing about school participation.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih prefers the reading club because members compare stories. Ayuk prefers the environmental club because he enjoys organising practical projects. Bih asks whether the groups could share an exhibition. Ayuk suggests checking space and supervision first. Their preferences remain different, while the proposal creates a possible shared task.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Prepare short turns: state the point, give a relevant reason and invite a response. Use fictional people if the subject is private. Practise with a partner when available; written choices here do not establish oral fluency or listening ability. Challenge an idea without insulting the speaker.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: One preference proves every learner wants the same activity. Correction: A preference describes the speaker’s view, not a universal fact.
Any unrelated statement supports the view equally. Correction: The reason must bear on the preference.
Clarification means changing to an unrelated topic. Correction: It makes the present proposal clearer.
A proposal proves the event already happened. Correction: It suggests a possible action, not a completed event.
